Load referenced resources only as needed. # Visualize Build small interactive surfaces the user can explore right inside the chat: parameter-driven simulations, algorithm walkthroughs, charts and plots, side-by-side comparisons, and product-screen mockups. The `visualize` tool renders your markup as a live sandboxed card in the conversation, or, for something to work in rather than glance at, as a full page in its own tab. - Reach for a card when seeing or manipulating something answers the question better than prose would. A request that merely mentions data or a web page does not by itself call for one. - When the user asks for a real deliverable — a website, a page in their app, a component, a standalone file — build project files instead; that is not an in-conversation card. - When a static labeled diagram of nodes and edges already tells the whole story, emit a fenced Mermaid block and skip the tool. The card earns its place through motion, interaction, or adjustable inputs. ## Resources Read from this skill's resource directory as the task demands — before your first chart, read `references/charts.md`; before styling anything, read `references/design.md`: - `references/design.md` — taste, theme tokens, base classes, layout. - `references/charts.md` — Chart.js-first charting, theme-color resolution, hand-rolled SVG rules, entrance animation recipes. - `examples/interactive-simulator.html` — sliders wired with `dshViz.bind` driving a `dshViz.chart` area curve: theme colors, gradient fill, in-place updates, kept settings. The template for any standard chart. - `examples/comparison-chart.html` — a hand-rolled SVG comparison with direct labels and a hover detail. The template for custom visuals only. ## Calling the tool Pass the markup directly as the `fragment` argument, with an optional `title` and optional `mode`. The card starts rendering while you are still generating, and a copy of the finished fragment is saved outside the user's project, in this conversation's own card store; the result names its `path`. Never write the fragment into the workspace yourself. ## Choosing the surface - `inline` (default): the card answers the question at hand, fits the chat column, and stays within about one and a half screens. - `wide`: several compact panels must sit side by side to be compared. A single dense chart stays inline. - `page`: the user will *use* the thing rather than glance at it in passing — a multi-view tool, a dashboard with filters, a full-screen simulation, map, 3D scene or large graph, a long multi-step walkthrough, a full desktop mockup — or they ask for a separate page or full screen. The chat shows a launcher card with a live thumbnail; the user opens the page in its own tab. Pass a `summary`: one short line saying what the page lets them do. A page is still a fragment under every rule below, not a project file. If they want a page *in their app* or a file to keep, build project files. ## Page layout Design a `page` for a desktop browser tab (1280px and wider, any height), not the chat column: - Wrap it as `

` (a centred container; add `viz-page-narrow` for reading-width content). Group content in `
` with its own heading. - Several views go behind tabs: `.viz-tabs` holding `
